title: "Gaussian concentration models on a fixed graph"

  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Gaussian concentration models on a fixed graph}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(gAtoms)
```

`fit_gaussian_graph()` estimates a Gaussian concentration matrix whose off-diagonal
zeros are specified by an undirected graph. Supply observations in rows and
variables in columns. Named data columns are matched to named graph vertices;
otherwise columns follow graph order.

```{r fit}
set.seed(42)
G <- igraph::make_ring(5, circular = FALSE)
X <- matrix(rnorm(1000), 200, 5)
dec <- atom_decompose(G)
fit <- fit_gaussian_graph(X, graph = G, decomp = dec)
fit
summary(fit)
logLik(fit)
AIC(fit)
BIC(fit)
precision(fit)
vcov(fit)
```

Complete atoms use exact Cholesky closed form. Incomplete atoms use the optional
gRim package by default (`engine = "gRim"`, the default) or `engine = "ggm"` for
the optional ggm adapter; the requested engine is used as given. gRim defaults to
NCD and can retry covips after nonconvergence. ggm has
no iteration-limit argument and requires positive definite local empirical
covariances. No fitting path in this API adds ridge regularization.
gRim supplies both `K` and `Sigma`; ggm supplies `Shat`, used as `Sigma`,
and its adapter computes `K` by one Cholesky inversion. The returned covariance
is retained after numerical cleanup of precision nonedges.

Statistics are computed once: centered SSD divided by **n**, not n-1. With
`mean = "zero"`, the observations are not centered. The Gaussian module
currently requires complete finite observations.

The sparse precision matrix is assembled by adding atom blocks and subtracting
ordered separator blocks. Default covariance reconstruction uses the perfect
ordering and canonical separator covariances. Set `covariance = "none"` to
avoid storing a dense global covariance; `vcov()` then returns `NULL`.
`covariance = "solve"` provides a direct inverse for small diagnostic problems.
`vcov()` describes the fitted variables, not uncertainty of estimated parameters.

Local failures raise an `atom_gaussian_error` condition carrying `status`,
`atom_id` and `vertices`. Nonconvergence is not evidence of MLE nonexistence.
Deviance is unavailable if the saturated empirical covariance is singular,
even when the graph-constrained fit succeeds. See `fit$diagnostics$deviance`.

`logLik()` includes the Gaussian normalizing constant. Its parameter count is
p+m for concentration parameters plus p when estimating the mean. AIC and BIC
use that count and the number of supplied observations.
